item.title: Genetic network shaping Kenyon cell identity and function in <i>Drosophila</i> mushroom bodies
item.description: Revealing the molecular mechanisms underlying neuronal specification and acquisition of specific functions is key to understanding how the nervous system is constructed. In the Drosophila brain, Kenyon cells (KCs) are sequentially generated to assemble the backbone of the mushroom body (MB). item.title: A sense of direction
item.description: Migratory moths use both magnetic and visual cues for navigation when travelling long distances in the dark.

item.title: Agent-based modeling reveals how bats navigate dense group emergences
item.description: Bats face a complex navigation challenge when emerging from densely populated roosts, where vast numbers take off at once in dark, confined spaces. Each bat must avoid collisions with walls and conspecifics while locating the exit, all amidst overlapping acoustic signals. This crowded environment creates the risk of acoustic jamming, in which the calls of neighboring bats interfere with echo detection, potentially obscuring vital information. item.title: Raw signal segmentation for estimating RNA modification from Nanopore direct RNA sequencing data
item.description: Estimating RNA modifications from Nanopore direct RNA sequencing data is a critical task for the RNA research community. However, current computational methods often fail to deliver satisfactory results due to inaccurate segmentation of the raw signal. We have developed a new method, SegPore, which leverages a molecular jiggling translocation hypothesis to improve raw signal segmentation. item.title: Resolving synaptic events using subsynaptically targeted GCaMP8 variants
item.description: While genetically encoded Ca2+ indicators are valuable for visualizing neural activity, their speed and sensitivity have had limited performance when compared to chemical dyes and electrophysiology, particularly at synaptic compartments. item.title: JAX Animal Behavior System (JABS), a genetics-informed, end-to-end advanced behavioral phenotyping platform for the laboratory mouse
item.description: Automated detection of complex animal behavior remains a challenge in neuroscience. item.title: Sperm motility in mice with oligo-astheno-teratozoospermia restored by in vivo injection and electroporation of naked mRNA
item.description: Oligo-astheno-teratozoospermia (OAT), a recurrent cause of male infertility, is the most frequent disorder of spermatogenesis with a predominantly genetic origin. Patients and mice bearing mutations in the ARMC2 gene exhibit reduced sperm concentration, multiple morphological defects, and impaired motility, defining a canonical OAT phenotype. item.title: Toward neuroanatomical and cognitive foundations of macaque social tolerance grades
item.description: The macaque genus includes 25 species with diverse social systems, ranging from low to high social tolerance grades. Such interspecific behavioral variability provides a unique model to tackle the evolutionary foundation of primate social brain. Yet, the neuroanatomical correlates of these social tolerance grades remain unknown. item.description: The brain is thought to optimise behaviour by generating predictions based on learned statistical regularities. item.title: Intracellular expression of a fluorogenic DNA aptamer using retron Eco2
item.description: DNA aptamers are short, single-stranded DNA molecules that bind specifically to a range of targets such as proteins, cells, and small molecules. Typically, they are utilized in the development of therapeutic agents, diagnostics, drug delivery systems, and biosensors.
